references.authors: Zhang Y, Talalay P, Cho CG, et al.
references.title: A major inducer of anticarcinogenic protective enzymes from broccoli: isolation and elucidation of structure.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Isolated sulforaphane from broccoli as a major, very potent inducer of phase 2 detoxication enzymes (quinone reductase, GSTs) that does not induce phase 1 cytochromes P450.

references.authors: Fahey JW, Zhang Y, Talalay P
references.title: Broccoli sprouts: an exceptionally rich source of inducers of enzymes that protect against chemical carcinogens.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Three-day-old broccoli sprouts contain 10-100 times more glucoraphanin than mature plants and negligible indole glucosinolates; sprout extracts reduced DMBA mammary tumours in rats.

references.authors: Dinkova-Kostova AT, Holtzclaw WD, Cole RN, et al.
references.title: Direct evidence that sulfhydryl groups of Keap1 are the sensors regulating induction of phase 2 enzymes that protect against carcinogens and oxidants.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Showed directly that inducers such as sulforaphane react with the most reactive of KEAP1's 25 cysteine thiols, disrupting the KEAP1-Nrf2 complex so Nrf2 can activate ARE-driven genes.

references.authors: Hu C, Eggler AL, Mesecar AD, et al.
references.title: Modification of keap1 cysteine residues by sulforaphane.
references.finding: Mass spectrometry with a corrected protocol confirmed that KEAP1 cysteine 151 is among the residues most readily (and reversibly) modified by sulforaphane.

references.authors: Kobayashi A, Kang MI, Okawa H, et al.
references.title: Oxidative stress sensor Keap1 functions as an adaptor for Cul3-based E3 ligase to regulate proteasomal degradation of Nrf2.
references.finding: KEAP1 is the adaptor of a Cul3 E3 ubiquitin ligase that keeps Nrf2 half-life under 20 minutes by sending it to the proteasome.

references.authors: Heiss E, Herhaus C, Klimo K, et al.
references.title: Nuclear factor kappa B is a molecular target for sulforaphane-mediated anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
references.finding: In LPS-stimulated macrophages, sulforaphane cut NO, PGE2 and TNF-alpha by selectively reducing NF-kB DNA binding without blocking IkB degradation or NF-kB nuclear entry.

references.authors: Myzak MC, Tong P, Dashwood WM, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane retards the growth of human PC-3 xenografts and inhibits HDAC activity in human subjects.
references.finding: A single 68 g serving of broccoli sprouts inhibited histone deacetylase (HDAC) activity in blood mononuclear cells at 3 and 6 h; sulforaphane also slowed prostate cancer xenografts in mice.

references.authors: Dinkova-Kostova AT, Fahey JW, Kostov RV, et al.
references.title: KEAP1 and Done? Targeting the NRF2 Pathway with Sulforaphane.
references.finding: Of the many proposed cellular targets of sulforaphane, only KEAP1-Nrf2 signalling can be considered validated; summarises animal carcinogenesis protection and short-term clinical endpoints.

references.authors: Yagishita Y, Gatbonton-Schwager TN, McCallum ML, et al.
references.title: Current Landscape of NRF2 Biomarkers in Clinical Trials.
references.finding: Reviews NRF2 biomarkers in trials of dimethyl fumarate, bardoxolone, oltipraz and sulforaphane; no biomarker yet excels at defining pharmacodynamic action in humans.

references.authors: Calabrese EJ, Kozumbo WJ
references.title: The hormetic dose-response mechanism: Nrf2 activation.
references.finding: Argues Nrf2 mediates hormetic dose responses and is quantitatively constrained, producing modest maximal stimulation rather than open-ended increases.

references.authors: Bao Y, Wang W, Zhou Z, et al.
references.title: Benefits and risks of the hormetic effects of dietary isothiocyanates on cancer prevention.
references.finding: Sulforaphane was biphasic in cell culture: 1-5 µM increased proliferation and migration of several human cell lines (including cancer cells) while 10-40 µM inhibited them.

references.authors: Saw CL, Cintrón M, Wu TY, et al.
references.title: Pharmacodynamics of dietary phytochemical indoles I3C and DIM: Induction of Nrf2-mediated phase II drug metabolizing and antioxidant genes and synergism with isothiocyanates.
references.finding: In HepG2 cells, low concentrations of crucifer indoles (I3C, DIM) combined with sulforaphane or PEITC induced ARE-driven genes additively or synergistically.

references.authors: Cuadrado A, Rojo AI, Wells G, et al.
references.title: Therapeutic targeting of the NRF2 and KEAP1 partnership in chronic diseases.
references.finding: NRF2 activation is cytoprotective in many chronic disease models, but target specificity, pharmacodynamics, efficacy and safety remain unresolved challenges for therapeutic activators.

references.authors: Houghton CA, Fassett RG, Coombes JS
references.title: Sulforaphane and Other Nutrigenomic Nrf2 Activators: Can the Clinician's Expectation Be Matched by the Reality?
references.finding: Sulforaphane activates Nrf2 more potently and is far more bioavailable than curcumin, silymarin or resveratrol supplements.

references.authors: Ye L, Dinkova-Kostova AT, Wade KL, et al.
references.title: Quantitative determination of dithiocarbamates in human plasma, serum, erythrocytes and urine: pharmacokinetics of broccoli sprout isothiocyanates in humans.
references.finding: After ~200 µmol broccoli sprout isothiocyanates, plasma levels peaked at 0.9-2.3 µM at 1 h and fell with a half-life of 1.77 h; 58% of the dose was excreted in urine within 8 h.

references.authors: Shapiro TA, Fahey JW, Wade KL, et al.
references.title: Chemoprotective glucosinolates and isothiocyanates of broccoli sprouts: metabolism and excretion in humans.
references.finding: Isothiocyanates were about 6x more bioavailable than glucosinolates; excretion was linear from 25 to 200 µmol with low variation on repeated dosing; chewing sprouts thoroughly raised excretion (42 vs 29 µmol).

references.authors: Shapiro TA, Fahey JW, Dinkova-Kostova AT, et al.
references.title: Safety, tolerance, and metabolism of broccoli sprout glucosinolates and isothiocyanates: a clinical phase I study.
references.finding: Glucosinolate extracts (25 or 100 µmol every 8 h for 7 days) converted ~18-20% vs ~71% for isothiocyanate extracts; no toxicity in 32 blood tests including liver enzymes and thyroid hormones.

references.authors: Conaway CC, Getahun SM, Liebes LL, et al.
references.title: Disposition of glucosinolates and sulforaphane in humans after ingestion of steamed and fresh broccoli.
references.finding: After 200 g broccoli, 32% of isothiocyanates were excreted from fresh vs 10% from steamed broccoli, a roughly 3-fold difference.

references.authors: Vermeulen M, Klöpping-Ketelaars IW, van den Berg R, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability and kinetics of sulforaphane in humans after consumption of cooked versus raw broccoli.
references.finding: Sulforaphane bioavailability was 37% from raw vs 3.4% from cooked broccoli; plasma peak at 1.6 vs 6 h; excretion half-life about 2.5 h for both.

references.authors: Matusheski NV, Juvik JA, Jeffery EH
references.title: Heating decreases epithiospecifier protein activity and increases sulforaphane formation in broccoli.
references.finding: Heating broccoli to 60 °C before crushing increased sulforaphane and decreased the inactive nitrile by inactivating epithiospecifier protein; 70 °C and above reduced both in florets.

references.authors: Fahey JW, Wehage SL, Holtzclaw WD, et al.
references.title: Protection of humans by plant glucosinolates: efficiency of conversion of glucosinolates to isothiocyanates by the gastrointestinal microflora.
references.finding: Gut-microbial conversion of glucoraphanin varied from ~1% to >40% between people but was consistent within a person; preformed isothiocyanates gave 70-90%; antibiotics and bowel cleansing abolish conversion.

references.authors: Egner PA, Chen JG, Wang JB, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability of Sulforaphane from two broccoli sprout beverages: results of a short-term, cross-over clinical trial in Qidong, China.
references.finding: A sulforaphane-rich beverage gave ~70% urinary recovery vs ~5% for a glucoraphanin-rich beverage, with less inter-individual variation; glucoraphanin gave slower, steadier exposure.

references.authors: Clarke JD, Hsu A, Riedl K, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability and inter-conversion of sulforaphane and erucin in human subjects consuming broccoli sprouts or broccoli supplement in a cross-over study design.
references.finding: A myrosinase-free broccoli supplement produced dramatically lower and later plasma and urinary sulforaphane and erucin than 40 g fresh broccoli sprouts.

references.authors: Clarke JD, Riedl K, Bella D, et al.
references.title: Comparison of isothiocyanate metabolite levels and histone deacetylase activity in human subjects consuming broccoli sprouts or broccoli supplement.
references.finding: Fresh sprouts gave higher, earlier isothiocyanate excretion than a myrosinase-free supplement with equal glucosinolate, and only sprouts lowered blood-cell HDAC activity.

references.authors: Cramer JM, Teran-Garcia M, Jeffery EH
references.title: Enhancing sulforaphane absorption and excretion in healthy men through the combined consumption of fresh broccoli sprouts and a glucoraphanin-rich powder.
references.finding: Combining fresh sprouts (70 µmol) with a myrosinase-free glucoraphanin powder recovered 65% of the dose as urinary SF-NAC vs 60% for sprouts alone and 24% for the powder alone.

references.authors: Fahey JW, Holtzclaw WD, Wehage SL, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane Bioavailability from Glucoraphanin-Rich Broccoli: Control by Active Endogenous Myrosinase.
references.finding: Sprouts or seeds given with their own active myrosinase yielded 3-4x more sulforaphane than glucoraphanin without active myrosinase; a commercial glucoraphanin supplement matched a boiled sprout extract.

references.authors: Atwell LL, Hsu A, Wong CP, et al.
references.title: Absorption and chemopreventive targets of sulforaphane in humans following consumption of broccoli sprouts or a myrosinase-treated broccoli sprout extract.
references.finding: At 200 µmol/day, fresh sprouts gave ~3x higher sulforaphane metabolites than a myrosinase-treated extract; splitting the dose prolonged exposure; no dose response in HO-1, HDAC activity or p21.

references.authors: Sivapalan T, Melchini A, Saha S, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability of Glucoraphanin and Sulforaphane from High-Glucoraphanin Broccoli.
references.finding: Soups (myrosinase denatured) from high-glucoraphanin broccoli gave 3-5x more circulating sulforaphane; excretion was 2-15% of glucoraphanin eaten, varying by person.

references.authors: Okunade O, Niranjan K, Ghawi SK, et al.
references.title: Supplementation of the Diet by Exogenous Myrosinase via Mustard Seeds to Increase the Bioavailability of Sulforaphane in Healthy Human Subjects after the Consumption of Cooked Broccoli.
references.finding: Adding 1 g brown mustard powder to 200 g cooked broccoli raised urinary SF-NAC from 9.8 to 44.7 µmol/g creatinine (over 4-fold).

references.authors: Fahey JW, Wade KL, Stephenson KK, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability of Sulforaphane Following Ingestion of Glucoraphanin-Rich Broccoli Sprout and Seed Extracts with Active Myrosinase: A Pilot Study of the Effects of Proton Pump Inhibitor Administration.
references.finding: With a glucoraphanin plus active-myrosinase seed/sprout extract, omeprazole (less stomach acid) and enteric coating increased conversion; greater body mass reduced conversion; cytoprotective PBMC genes rose with bioavailability.

references.authors: Mastaloudis A, Holcomb L, Fahey JW, et al.
references.title: Exogenous myrosinase from mustard seed increases bioavailability of sulforaphane from a glucoraphanin-rich broccoli seed extract in a randomized clinical study.
references.finding: Adding mustard-seed myrosinase to a glucoraphanin-rich broccoli seed extract doubled sulforaphane bioavailability (39.8% vs 18.6%); bacterial glucoraphanin-converting genes correlated with conversion.

references.authors: Fahey JW, Wade KL, Wehage SL, et al.
references.title: Stabilized sulforaphane for clinical use: Phytochemical delivery efficiency.
references.finding: Stabilised sulforaphane preparations (cyclodextrin and a commercial supplement) were as bioavailable as pure sulforaphane, peaking at about 2 h, but 6 of 10 volunteers reported mild stomach upset with one form.

references.authors: Liou CS, Sirk SJ, Diaz CAC, et al.
references.title: A Metabolic Pathway for Activation of Dietary Glucosinolates by a Human Gut Symbiont.
references.finding: Identified the Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron operon (BT2159-BT2156) that converts dietary glucosinolates to isothiocyanates in the gut.

references.authors: Gasper AV, Al-Janobi A, Smith JA, et al.
references.title: Glutathione S-transferase M1 polymorphism and metabolism of sulforaphane from standard and high-glucosinolate broccoli.
references.finding: GSTM1-null people had slightly higher plasma sulforaphane AUC and faster, larger urinary excretion than GSTM1-positive people; high-glucosinolate broccoli gave ~3x more sulforaphane.

references.authors: Steck SE, Gammon MD, Hebert JR, et al.
references.title: GSTM1, GSTT1, GSTP1, and GSTA1 polymorphisms and urinary isothiocyanate metabolites following broccoli consumption in humans.
references.finding: After a standard broccoli meal, GST genotypes did not substantially change isothiocyanate excretion; unexpectedly more GSTM1-null people were high excreters (62% vs 39%).

references.authors: London SJ, Yuan JM, Chung FL, et al.
references.title: Isothiocyanates, glutathione S-transferase M1 and T1 polymorphisms, and lung-cancer risk: a prospective study of men in Shanghai, China.
references.finding: Detectable urinary isothiocyanates predicted lower lung cancer risk (RR 0.65), most strongly in GSTM1-null (RR 0.36) and GSTM1/GSTT1 double-null men (RR 0.28).

references.authors: Charron CS, Vinyard BT, Ross SA, et al.
references.title: Absorption and metabolism of isothiocyanates formed from broccoli glucosinolates: effects of BMI and daily consumption in a randomised clinical trial.
references.finding: Fifteen days of daily broccoli did not uniformly change isothiocyanate absorption: it rose in leaner people (BMI <26) and fell in heavier people; GSTM1 genotype had no effect.

references.authors: Yagishita Y, Fahey JW, Dinkova-Kostova AT, et al.
references.title: Broccoli or Sulforaphane: Is It the Source or Dose That Matters?
references.finding: Reviews >50 clinical trials; supermarket broccoli averaged 0.38 µmol glucoraphanin/g (range <0.005-1.13); dose-response shapes and a maximally effective dose are not established.

references.authors: Saito A, Ishikawa S, Yang K, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane as a potential therapeutic agent: a comprehensive analysis of clinical trials and mechanistic insights.
references.finding: Of 84 registered sulforaphane/broccoli-extract trials only 39 were published, raising publication-bias concerns; summarises effects by disease category.

references.authors: Kensler TW, Chen JG, Egner PA, et al.
references.title: Effects of glucosinolate-rich broccoli sprouts on urinary levels of aflatoxin-DNA adducts and phenanthrene tetraols in a randomized clinical trial in He Zuo township, Qidong, People's Republic of China.
references.finding: Nightly broccoli sprout infusion (400 µmol glucoraphanin) for 2 weeks did not change aflatoxin-DNA adducts between arms, but higher sulforaphane excretion correlated with fewer adducts and phenanthrene tetraols.

references.authors: Kensler TW, Ng D, Carmella SG, et al.
references.title: Modulation of the metabolism of airborne pollutants by glucoraphanin-rich and sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout beverages in Qidong, China.
references.finding: Seven days of sulforaphane-rich or glucoraphanin-rich sprout beverage raised excretion of glutathione conjugates of acrolein, crotonaldehyde and benzene by 20-50% vs baseline, with no difference between beverages.

references.authors: Egner PA, Chen JG, Zarth AT, et al.
references.title: Rapid and sustainable detoxication of airborne pollutants by broccoli sprout beverage: results of a randomized clinical trial in China.
references.finding: Daily 600 µmol glucoraphanin + 40 µmol sulforaphane for 12 weeks raised excretion of benzene (+61%) and acrolein (+23%) conjugates vs placebo; sulforaphane bioavailability did not decline over 12 weeks.

references.authors: Chen JG, Johnson J, Egner P, et al.
references.title: Dose-dependent detoxication of the airborne pollutant benzene in a randomized trial of broccoli sprout beverage in Qidong, China.
references.finding: Only the full-dose beverage (median 24.6 µmol urinary sulforaphane metabolites/day) raised benzene mercapturic acid (+63%); half (+11%) and one-fifth (-6%) doses did not differ from placebo.

references.authors: Riedl MA, Saxon A, Diaz-Sanchez D
references.title: Oral sulforaphane increases Phase II antioxidant enzymes in the human upper airway.
references.finding: Broccoli sprout homogenate dose-dependently induced GSTM1, GSTP1, NQO1 and HO-1 mRNA in nasal cells, maximal at 200 g sprouts; alfalfa sprouts had no effect.

references.authors: Heber D, Li Z, Garcia-Lloret M, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout extract attenuates nasal allergic response to diesel exhaust particles.
references.finding: Four days of a broccoli sprout extract delivering 100 µmol sulforaphane cut the nasal white-cell response to a diesel exhaust particle challenge by about half.

references.authors: Noah TL, Zhang H, Zhou H, et al.
references.title: Effect of broccoli sprouts on nasal response to live attenuated influenza virus in smokers: a randomized, double-blind study.
references.finding: Four days of broccoli sprout homogenate reduced post-vaccine nasal IL-6 and influenza virus quantity and raised NQO1 in smokers; trends in nonsmokers were not significant.

references.authors: Duran CG, Burbank AJ, Mills KH, et al.
references.title: A proof-of-concept clinical study examining the NRF2 activator sulforaphane against neutrophilic airway inflammation.
references.finding: Broccoli sprout homogenate did not induce antioxidant genes or protect against neutrophilic airway inflammation after ozone exposure.

references.authors: Sudini K, Diette GB, Breysse PN, et al.
references.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of the Effect of Broccoli Sprouts on Antioxidant Gene Expression and Airway Inflammation in Asthmatics.
references.finding: Eating 100 g broccoli sprouts daily for 3 days did not reduce exhaled NO, improve lung function or induce antioxidant genes in nasal or blood cells.

references.authors: Wise RA, Holbrook JT, Criner G, et al.
references.title: Lack of Effect of Oral Sulforaphane Administration on Nrf2 Expression in COPD: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled Trial.
references.finding: 25 or 150 µmol/day sulforaphane for 4 weeks was absorbed but did not induce Nrf2 target genes in lung cells or change oxidative stress, inflammation or lung function.

references.authors: Yusin J, Wang V, Henning SM, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Broccoli Sprout Extract on Seasonal Grass Pollen-Induced Allergic Rhinitis.
references.finding: Broccoli sprout extract for 3 weeks improved peak nasal inspiratory flow after pollen challenge, mainly when combined with a nasal steroid; nasal cytokines did not change.

references.authors: Axelsson AS, Tubbs E, Mecham B, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane reduces hepatic glucose production and improves glucose control in patients with type 2 diabetes.
references.finding: Broccoli sprout extract (150 µmol sulforaphane/day, 12 weeks) reduced fasting blood glucose and HbA1c in obese patients with dysregulated type 2 diabetes (not in the whole group); in cells and animals sulforaphane suppressed hepatic gluconeogenesis via NRF2.

references.authors: Dwibedi C, Axelsson AS, Abrahamsson B, et al.
references.title: Effect of broccoli sprout extract and baseline gut microbiota on fasting blood glucose in prediabetes: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
references.finding: 150 µmol/day broccoli sprout extract for 12 weeks missed its primary target (fasting glucose -0.2 mmol/L vs placebo, P=0.04); responders had gut Bacteroides genes for glucoraphanin conversion; GI side effects were more common.

references.authors: Bahadoran Z, Mirmiran P, Hosseinpanah F, et al.
references.title: Broccoli sprouts reduce oxidative stress in type 2 diabetes: a randomized double-blind clinical trial.
references.finding: 5-10 g/day broccoli sprout powder for 4 weeks lowered MDA, oxidized LDL and an oxidative stress index and raised total antioxidant capacity.

references.authors: Bahadoran Z, Tohidi M, Nazeri P, et al.
references.title: Effect of broccoli sprouts on insulin resistance in type 2 diabetic patients: a randomized double-blind clinical trial.
references.finding: 10 g/day broccoli sprout powder for 4 weeks lowered serum insulin and HOMA-IR (P=0.05).

references.authors: Bahadoran Z, Mirmiran P, Hosseinpanah F, et al.
references.title: Broccoli sprouts powder could improve serum triglyceride and oxidized LDL/LDL-cholesterol ratio in type 2 diabetic patients: a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial.
references.finding: 10 g/day broccoli sprout powder for 4 weeks lowered triglycerides, the oxidized LDL/LDL ratio and the atherogenic index.

references.authors: Armah CN, Derdemezis C, Traka MH, et al.
references.title: Diet rich in high glucoraphanin broccoli reduces plasma LDL cholesterol: Evidence from randomised controlled trials.
references.finding: 400 g/week of high-glucoraphanin broccoli for 12 weeks lowered LDL cholesterol by 5-7%, more than standard broccoli (2-3%, not significant).

references.authors: Christiansen B, Bellostas Muguerza N, Petersen AM, et al.
references.title: Ingestion of broccoli sprouts does not improve endothelial function in humans with hypertension.
references.finding: 10 g/day dried broccoli sprouts for 4 weeks did not improve flow-mediated dilation or blood pressure.

references.authors: Singh K, Connors SL, Macklin EA, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane treatment of autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: 50-150 µmol/day sulforaphane for 18 weeks improved Aberrant Behavior Checklist by 34% and Social Responsiveness Scale by 17% vs <3.3% on placebo; scores reverted after stopping.

references.authors: Bent S, Lawton B, Warren T, et al.
references.title: Identification of urinary metabolites that correlate with clinical improvements in children with autism treated with sulforaphane from broccoli.
references.finding: In a 12-week open-label study, Social Responsiveness Scale improved (-9.7 points) but the ABC change was not significant; 77 urinary metabolites correlated with clinical change.

references.authors: Momtazmanesh S, Amirimoghaddam-Yazdi Z, Moghaddam HS, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane as an adjunctive treatment for irritability in children with autism spectrum disorder: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
references.finding: Sulforaphane (50 or 100 µmol/day by weight) added to risperidone for 10 weeks improved irritability and hyperactivity vs placebo, without differences in other ABC subscales or adverse events.

references.authors: Zimmerman AW, Singh K, Connors SL, et al.
references.title: Randomized controlled trial of sulforaphane and metabolite discovery in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
references.finding: 15 weeks of sulforaphane did not significantly improve the primary clinician scale (Cohen's d 0.21, CI crossing zero); caregiver ABC improved (d -0.96) but SRS-2 did not.

references.authors: Magner M, Thorová K, Župová V, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane Treatment in Children with Autism: A Prospective Randomized Double-Blind Study.
references.finding: 50 µmol/day sulforaphane for 36 weeks produced no significant improvement in ADOS-2, SRS-2 or ABC vs placebo.

references.authors: Ou J, Smith RC, Tobe RH, et al.
references.title: Efficacy of Sulforaphane in Treatment of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Multi-center Trial.
references.finding: In a multicentre trial in China, caregiver-rated scales did not differ from placebo while clinician-rated scales improved; sulforaphane was well tolerated.

references.authors: Wang R, Ren Z, Li Y
references.title: The effect of sulforaphane on autism spectrum disorder: systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Pooled ASD trials showed small improvements in total symptoms (SMD -0.27) and aberrant behaviour (SMD -0.43) with no excess adverse events; results depended on assessors and tools.

references.authors: Dickerson F, Origoni A, Katsafanas E, et al.
references.title: Randomized controlled trial of an adjunctive sulforaphane nutraceutical in schizophrenia.
references.finding: 100 µmol/day adjunctive sulforaphane for 18 weeks had no significant effect on symptoms or cognition (as summarised by a 2025 meta-analysis).

references.authors: Hei G, Smith RC, Li R, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane Effects on Cognition and Symptoms in First and Early Episode Schizophrenia: A Randomized Double-Blind Trial.
references.finding: Two sulforaphane doses for 22 weeks did not improve the primary MATRICS composite or PANSS, though some cognitive domains (working memory, verbal learning) improved.

references.authors: Huang J, Chen A, Jin H, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and Safety of Sulforaphane Added to Antipsychotics for the Treatment of Negative Symptoms of Schizophrenia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
references.finding: 24 weeks of high-dose sulforaphane (Avmacol Extra Strength) added to antipsychotics reduced PANSS negative symptoms more than placebo.

references.authors: Chen H, Lu J, Zou T, et al.
references.title: Effects of sulforaphane on negative symptoms and cognitive impairments in chronic schizophrenia patients: A randomized double-blind trial.
references.finding: 24 weeks of sulforaphane reduced PANSS negative symptom scores vs placebo but did not improve MATRICS cognition.

references.authors: Kassar O, M Mansour ME, Farag N, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and safety of sulforaphane in schizophrenia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Sulforaphane did not improve PANSS total or positive scores; a small negative-symptom benefit at 12 weeks (MD -1.06) was not sustained; lipids improved and discontinuation was lower.

references.authors: Okazaki M, Sakuma K, Jo H, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and safety of Nrf2 activators for schizophrenia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Across Nrf2 activators in schizophrenia (vitamin C, curcumin, resveratrol, sulforaphane), sulforaphane lowered all-cause discontinuation and some lipids; curcumin showed only marginal, non-robust symptom benefit.

references.authors: Ghazizadeh-Hashemi F, Bagheri S, Ashraf-Ganjouei A, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and safety of sulforaphane for treatment of mild to moderate depression in patients with history of cardiac interventions: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
references.finding: Six weeks of sulforaphane improved HAM-D scores and response rate (30% vs 6.7%) vs placebo; remission difference was not significant.

references.authors: Nouchi R, Hu Q, Saito T, et al.
references.title: Brain Training and Sulforaphane Intake Interventions Separately Improve Cognitive Performance in Healthy Older Adults, Whereas a Combination of These Interventions Does Not Have More Beneficial Effects: Evidence from a Randomized Controlled Trial.
references.finding: 30 mg (~69 µmol) glucoraphanin daily for 12 weeks improved processing speed and working memory vs placebo; combining with brain training added nothing.

references.authors: Nouchi R, Hu Q, Ushida Y, et al.
references.title: Effects of sulforaphane intake on processing speed and negative moods in healthy older adults: Evidence from a randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: Analysis of the same 12-week trial: glucoraphanin improved processing speed and reduced negative mood, without changes in oxidative stress, inflammation or neural plasticity biomarkers.

references.authors: Shimizu S, Kasai S, Suzuki C, et al.
references.title: Efficacy of 42-month oral administration of glucoraphanin in preventing cognitive decline in individuals at elevated risk of dementia, including those with mild cognitive impairment: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study.
references.finding: 30 mg/day glucoraphanin for 42 months gave greater improvement in memory performance index than placebo in a small pilot (19 completers).

references.authors: Galan MV, Kishan AA, Silverman AL
references.title: Oral broccoli sprouts for the treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection: a preliminary report.
references.finding: Broccoli sprouts twice daily for 7 days were followed by negative stool antigen in 7 of 9 patients, but durable eradication was confirmed in only about 3 of 9.

references.authors: Yanaka A, Fahey JW, Fukumoto A, et al.
references.title: Dietary sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprouts reduce colonization and attenuate gastritis in Helicobacter pylori-infected mice and humans.
references.finding: 70 g/day broccoli sprouts (420 µmol glucoraphanin) for 8 weeks lowered urea breath test, stool antigen and pepsinogens vs alfalfa sprouts; values returned to baseline 2 months after stopping.

references.authors: Chang YW, Jang JY, Kim YH, et al.
references.title: The Effects of Broccoli Sprout Extract Containing Sulforaphane on Lipid Peroxidation and Helicobacter pylori Infection in the Gastric Mucosa.
references.finding: Broccoli sprout extract did not reduce H. pylori density (urea breath test) but lowered gastric mucosal MDA.

references.authors: Chang YW, Park YM, Oh CH, et al.
references.title: Effects of probiotics or broccoli supplementation on Helicobacter pylori eradication with standard clarithromycin-based triple therapy.
references.finding: Adding sulforaphane to clarithromycin triple therapy did not raise H. pylori eradication rates (ITT 81.6% vs 85.2%).

references.authors: Talalay P, Fahey JW, Healy ZR, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane mobilizes cellular defenses that protect skin against damage by UV radiation.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Topical sulforaphane-rich sprout extract induced phase 2 enzymes in human skin and reduced UV-induced erythema by a mean 37.7%.

references.authors: Kerns ML, Guss L, Fahey J, et al.
references.title: Randomized, split-body, single-blinded clinical trial of topical broccoli sprout extract: Assessing the feasibility of its use in keratin-based disorders.
references.finding: Topical broccoli sprout extract activated Nrf2 and induced keratin 17 in human epidermis without altering keratins 5/14, supporting feasibility for epidermolysis bullosa simplex.

references.authors: Alumkal JJ, Slottke R, Schwartzman J, et al.
references.title: A phase II study of sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout extracts in men with recurrent prostate cancer.
references.n: 20 men with recurrent prostate cancer (single arm)
references.finding: 200 µmol/day sulforaphane-rich extract for up to 20 weeks did not produce >=50% PSA declines (1 of 20), but PSA doubling time lengthened from 6.1 to 9.6 months.

references.authors: Cipolla BG, Mandron E, Lefort JM, et al.
references.title: Effect of Sulforaphane in Men with Biochemical Recurrence after Radical Prostatectomy.
references.finding: 60 mg (~340 µmol) stabilised sulforaphane daily for 6 months missed the primary PSA-slope endpoint; PSA rose less (+0.10 vs +0.62 ng/mL) and doubling time was 86% longer than placebo.

references.authors: Zhang Z, Garzotto M, Davis EW 2nd, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane Bioavailability and Chemopreventive Activity in Men Presenting for Biopsy of the Prostate Gland: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
references.finding: 200 µmol/day broccoli sprout extract raised sulforaphane levels but did not change blood HDAC activity or prostate tissue biomarkers; 40 genes changed in expression.

references.authors: Traka MH, Melchini A, Coode-Bate J, et al.
references.title: Transcriptional changes in prostate of men on active surveillance after a 12-mo glucoraphanin-rich broccoli intervention-results from the Effect of Sulforaphane on prostate CAncer PrEvention (ESCAPE) randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: One 300 mL portion per week of high-glucoraphanin broccoli soup for 12 months attenuated cancer-associated gene expression changes in prostate tissue in a dose-dependent way.

references.authors: Atwell LL, Zhang Z, Mori M, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane Bioavailability and Chemopreventive Activity in Women Scheduled for Breast Biopsy.
references.finding: A glucoraphanin supplement for 2-8 weeks lowered blood-cell HDAC activity but did not change breast tissue biomarkers vs placebo.

references.authors: Tahata S, Singh SV, Lin Y, et al.
references.title: Evaluation of Biodistribution of Sulforaphane after Administration of Oral Broccoli Sprout Extract in Melanoma Patients with Multiple Atypical Nevi.
references.finding: 50, 100 or 200 µmol/day broccoli sprout extract for 28 days was well tolerated and gave dose-dependent plasma and skin sulforaphane levels.

references.authors: Lozanovski VJ, Polychronidis G, Gross W, et al.
references.title: Broccoli sprout supplementation in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer is difficult despite positive effects-results from the POUDER pilot study.
references.finding: Broccoli sprout capsules (508 µmol sulforaphane + 411 µmol glucoraphanin/day) were hard to tolerate (15 capsules, nausea, high drop-out); early survival trends favoured treatment but the pilot was underpowered.

references.authors: Yuan JM, Kensler TW, Dacic S, et al.
references.title: Randomized Phase II Clinical Trial of Sulforaphane in Former Smokers at High Risk for Lung Cancer.
references.finding: About 95 µmol/day sulforaphane for 12 months did not change bronchial histopathology but reduced the Ki-67 proliferation index (-20% vs +65% on placebo).

references.authors: ElKhalifa D, Al-Ziftawi N, Awaisu A, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and tolerability of sulforaphane in the therapeutic management of cancers: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Systematic review of sulforaphane in cancer patients: inconsistent PSA effects, some biomarker changes, no excess adverse events, heterogeneous dosing.

references.authors: Kikuchi M, Ushida Y, Shiozawa H, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout extract improves hepatic abnormalities in male subjects.
references.finding: Glucoraphanin-rich sprout extract capsules for 2 months lowered ALT, gamma-GTP and urinary 8-OHdG vs placebo.

references.authors: Satomi S, Takahashi S, Yoshida K, et al.
references.title: Effects of broccoli sprout supplements enriched in glucoraphanin on liver functions in healthy middle-aged adults with high-normal serum hepatic biomarkers: A randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: 60 mg (137 µmol) glucoraphanin daily for 24 weeks lowered serum ALT vs placebo without changing serum glutathione.

references.authors: López-Chillón MT, Carazo-Díaz C, Prieto-Merino D, et al.
references.title: Effects of long-term consumption of broccoli sprouts on inflammatory markers in overweight subjects.
references.finding: 30 g/day fresh broccoli sprouts for 10 weeks lowered IL-6 (4.76 to 2.11 pg/mL) and CRP in an uncontrolled before-after design.

references.authors: Navarro SL, Schwarz Y, Song X, et al.
references.title: Cruciferous vegetables have variable effects on biomarkers of systemic inflammation in a randomized controlled trial in healthy young adults.
references.finding: Double-dose crucifers (14 g/kg body weight) for 14 days lowered IL-6 by 19% vs a vegetable-free diet; no effect on CRP or TNF-alpha.

references.authors: van Steenwijk HP, Vinken A, van Osch FHM, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane as a potential modifier of calorie-induced inflammation: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial.
references.finding: 16 g broccoli sprouts before a high-calorie drink did not blunt the inflammatory response; CCL-2 rose slightly more.

references.authors: Komine S, Miura I, Miyashita N, et al.
references.title: Effect of a sulforaphane supplement on muscle soreness and damage induced by eccentric exercise in young adults: A pilot study.
references.finding: Two weeks of a sulforaphane supplement raised NQO1 mRNA in blood cells and reduced muscle soreness and serum MDA 2 days after eccentric exercise.

references.authors: Cesanelli L, Thomas R, Mickevičius M, et al.
references.title: Short-Term Effects of Broccoli-Derived Glucoraphanin on Recovery from Eccentric Muscle Damage: A Double-Blind Randomized Crossover Study.
references.finding: Two weeks of high-glucoraphanin broccoli powder (reconstituted in hot water) did not change recovery from eccentric muscle damage.

references.authors: Traustadóttir T, Islam H, Ostrom EL
references.title: Exercise and phytochemicals as modulators of redox homeostasis in aging.
references.finding: Exercise-induced Nrf2 activation weakens with age; evidence that adding Nrf2-activating phytochemicals (curcumin, sulforaphane, astaxanthin) to exercise helps older adults is insufficient.

references.authors: Volz N, Boettler U, Winkler S, et al.
references.title: Effect of coffee combining green coffee bean constituents with typical roasting products on the Nrf2/ARE pathway in vitro and in vivo.
references.finding: 750 mL/day of a specially roasted coffee for 4 weeks increased Nrf2 transcription in blood lymphocytes on average, with large inter-individual variation.

references.authors: Chartoumpekis DV, Ziros PG, Chen JG, et al.
references.title: Broccoli sprout beverage is safe for thyroid hormonal and autoimmune status: Results of a 12-week randomized trial.
references.finding: 84 days of a sulforaphane/glucoraphanin beverage did not change TSH, free T4, thyroglobulin or thyroid autoimmunity.

references.authors: Galanty A, Grudzińska M, Paździora W, et al.
references.title: Do Brassica Vegetables Affect Thyroid Function?-A Comprehensive Systematic Review.
references.finding: Systematic review: most evidence does not support antithyroid effects of Brassica vegetables in humans, especially with adequate iodine intake.

references.authors: Felker P, Bunch R, Leung AM
references.title: Concentrations of thiocyanate and goitrin in human plasma, their precursor concentrations in brassica vegetables, and associated potential risk for hypothyroidism.
references.finding: Goitrin inhibits thyroid iodine uptake at 194 but not 77 µmol; collards, Brussels sprouts and some Russian kale can contain that much, while commercial broccoli and kale contain <10 µmol per 100 g.

references.authors: Mahéo K, Morel F, Langouët S, et al.
references.title: Inhibition of cytochromes P-450 and induction of glutathione S-transferases by sulforaphane in primary human and rat hepatocytes.
references.finding: In primary human hepatocytes, sulforaphane induced GSTA1/2 and markedly decreased CYP3A4 expression and activity, while CYP1A2 was unaffected.

references.authors: Navarro SL, Peterson S, Chen C, et al.
references.title: Cruciferous vegetable feeding alters UGT1A1 activity: diet- and genotype-dependent changes in serum bilirubin in a controlled feeding trial.
references.finding: Cruciferous vegetable diets lowered serum bilirubin vs a vegetable-free diet, indicating induction of the drug-conjugating enzyme UGT1A1.

references.authors: Wakabayashi N, Itoh K, Wakabayashi J, et al.
references.title: Keap1-null mutation leads to postnatal lethality due to constitutive Nrf2 activation.
references.finding: Keap1-null mice, with constitutive Nrf2 activation, die after birth from oesophageal and forestomach hyperkeratosis; deleting Nrf2 rescues them.

references.authors: DeNicola GM, Karreth FA, Humpton TJ, et al.
references.title: Oncogene-induced Nrf2 transcription promotes ROS detoxification and tumorigenesis.
references.finding: Oncogenic Kras, Braf and Myc raise Nrf2 transcription to lower ROS, and Nrf2 is required for Kras-driven proliferation and tumorigenesis in mice.

references.authors: Wang XJ, Sun Z, Villeneuve NF, et al.
references.title: Nrf2 enhances resistance of cancer cells to chemotherapeutic drugs, the dark side of Nrf2.
references.finding: Nrf2 overexpression made cancer cells more resistant to cisplatin, doxorubicin and etoposide, while Nrf2 knock-down sensitised them.

references.authors: de Zeeuw D, Akizawa T, Audhya P, et al.
references.title: Bardoxolone methyl in type 2 diabetes and stage 4 chronic kidney disease.
references.finding: The synthetic Nrf2 activator bardoxolone methyl did not reduce kidney failure or CV death and increased heart-failure events (HR 1.83); the trial was stopped early.

references.authors: Valipour J, Nashtaei MS, Khosravizadeh Z, et al.
references.title: Effect of sulforaphane on apoptosis, reactive oxygen species and lipids peroxidation of human sperm during cryopreservation.
references.finding: Adding 5 µM sulforaphane to human sperm before freezing improved post-thaw viability, motility and morphology and lowered ROS and lipid peroxidation.

references.authors: Mu Y, Yin TL, Huang XX, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane ameliorates high-fat diet-induced spermatogenic deficiency in mice†.
references.finding: Sulforaphane injections reversed high-fat-diet-induced spermatogenic impairment in mice and, in vitro, protected mouse and human sperm motility from palmitic acid via AMPK-dependent ER-stress relief.

references.authors: Wang Y, Zhang Z, Guo W, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane reduction of testicular apoptotic cell death in diabetic mice is associated with the upregulation of Nrf2 expression and function.
references.finding: In diabetic mice, 4 months of sulforaphane prevented testicular cell death, oxidative damage and inflammation while up-regulating testicular Nrf2.

references.authors: Jiang XP, Tang JY, Xu Z, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane attenuates di-N-butylphthalate-induced reproductive damage in pubertal mice: Involvement of the Nrf2-antioxidant system.
references.finding: Sulforaphane attenuated phthalate (DBP)-induced falls in sperm count, motility and testosterone in pubertal mice via Nrf2.

references.authors: Taheri M, Hayati Roudbari N, Amidi F, et al.
references.title: The protective effect of sulforaphane against oxidative stress in granulosa cells of patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) through activation of AMPK/AKT/NRF2 signaling pathway.
references.n: granulosa cells from PCOS and control women (in vitro)
references.finding: Sulforaphane reduced ROS and apoptosis in granulosa-lutein cells from women with PCOS, with AMPK/AKT/NRF2 activation.

references.authors: Esfandyari S, Aleyasin A, Noroozi Z, et al.
references.title: The Protective Effect of Sulforaphane against Oxidative Stress through Activation of NRF2/ARE Pathway in Human Granulosa Cells.
references.finding: Sulforaphane pretreatment protected human granulosa cells from H2O2-induced ROS and apoptosis via NRF2, SOD and catalase.

references.authors: Sohel MMH, Konca Y, Akyuz B, et al.
references.title: Concentration dependent antioxidative and apoptotic effects of sulforaphane on bovine granulosa cells in vitro.
references.finding: In bovine granulosa cells, low sulforaphane (2 µM) activated NRF2 antioxidant genes while concentrations above ~15 µM were cytotoxic.

references.authors: Feng Z, Wang T, Sun Y, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane suppresses paraquat-induced oxidative damage in bovine in vitro-matured oocytes through Nrf2 transduction pathway.
references.finding: 1 µM sulforaphane during in vitro maturation raised bovine oocyte maturation and embryo rates and countered paraquat oxidative damage via Nrf2.

references.authors: Li WJ, Zhang X, Shen M, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane alleviates the meiosis defects induced by 3-nitropropionic acid in mouse oocytes.
references.finding: Sulforaphane alleviated 3-nitropropionic-acid-induced meiotic, spindle and mitochondrial defects in mouse oocytes matured in vitro.

references.authors: Zhang X, Shu XO, Xiang YB, et al.
references.title: Cruciferous vegetable consumption is associated with a reduced risk of total and cardiovascular disease mortality.
references.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of cruciferous vegetable intake was associated with 22% lower total mortality (HR 0.78), mainly cardiovascular, in the Shanghai cohorts.

references.authors: Li YZ, Yang ZY, Gong TT, et al.
references.title: Cruciferous vegetable consumption and multiple health outcomes: an umbrella review of 41 systematic reviews and meta-analyses of 303 observational studies.
references.finding: Umbrella review: cruciferous vegetable intake associated with lower risk of several cancers and all-cause mortality, but evidence was mostly weak to suggestive and observational.

references.authors: Aune D, Giovannucci E, Boffetta P, et al.
references.title: Fruit and vegetable intake and the risk of cardiovascular disease, total cancer and all-cause mortality-a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies.
references.finding: Per 200 g/day fruit and vegetables, all-cause mortality RR 0.90; cruciferous vegetables were among the types most strongly inversely associated with outcomes.
